literal: Even than ploughing, good indeed is applying manure; after weeding, even than watering, good is its protection.
translation: Applying manure is better than mere ploughing; and once weeding is done, guarding the crop is even more important than watering it.
modern: ஏர் பூட்டி உழுவதை விட எருவிடுவது நல்லது; களை எடுத்த பிறகு, நீர் பாய்ச்சுவதை விட பயிரைக் காவல் காப்பது நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet outlines the practical hierarchy of agricultural tasks to ensure a bountiful harvest. The author explains that while ploughing ('ஏர்') is the fundamental first step, applying manure ('எரு விடுதல்') is far more beneficial to the soil's fertility. Similarly, once the weeds are cleared ('கட்ட பின்'), protecting the growing crop ('காப்பு') from external threats is even more critical than watering it ('நீர்'). The verse emphasizes that consistent care and vigilant protection are the ultimate keys to farming success.
